requirements.requirement: At least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap is active on node1.
requirements.summary: Direct pre- and post-restart observations show /dev/zram0 active with 532,476 KiB usable capacity, a 545,259,520-byte backing size, and LZO compression.

requirements.requirement: The compressed in-memory swap activates automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: The service was enabled and healthy before restart. A bounded restart changed the boot identity, after which the system was running and the enabled service had recreated and activated /dev/zram0; current-boot logs directly confirm startup.

requirements.requirement: The compressed in-memory swap is preferred over disk-backed swap.
requirements.summary: Before and after restart, /dev/zram0 had priority 100 while disk-backed /dev/vda2 had priority -2, and direct assertions passed.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has more than 512 MiB of active LZO-compressed zram swap, it outranks the existing disk swap, and a directly observed restart demonstrated automatic recovery. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for the sole managed node: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart identity, running system state, and recovered swap service were all captured and independently corroborated by lifecycle observations.
limitations: Native package-manager consistency checks timed out both before and after execution, so package health could not be independently assessed. No package mutation was performed in the captured timeline.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating and enabling the script and service, activating it, correcting the initial marginal capacity shortfall, and restarting the node all had clear roles in implementing or validating the required outcome. The failed post-restart probes were read-only observations during expected downtime. No failed services, added network exposure, or abandoned temporary files were observed; lifecycle differences were normal restart-related identity, PID, and systemd-private-directory changes.
